content.title: Combining antiplatelets and OAC (excerpt)
content.summary: Recommendations for combining oral anticoagulants (OAC) and antiplatelet therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation and/or undergoing PCI after ACS.

recommendations.recommendation: Default strategy for patients with atrial fibrillation and CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥1 in men and ≥2 in women: after up to 1 week of triple antithrombotic therapy following the ACS event, use dual antithrombotic therapy consisting of a NOAC at the recommended stroke-prevention dose plus a single oral antiplatelet agent (preferably clopidogrel) for up to 12 months.

details.population: Patients with atrial fibrillation and recent ACS
details.initial_therapy: Up to 1 week of triple antithrombotic therapy after ACS

recommendations.recommendation: During PCI, give a UFH bolus in either of the following circumstances: if the patient is on a NOAC; or if the INR is <2.5 in VKA-treated patients.
If angiography within 24 h is anticipated, consider enoxaparin as an alternative to UFH.

details.context: Pre-angiography anticoagulation choice when angiography expected within 24 hours

notes: Prefer clopidogrel as the single oral antiplatelet agent when combining with a NOAC.
CHA2DS2-VASc is used to assess stroke risk and guide antithrombotic strategy.
INR thresholds relate to VKA-treated patients and guide need for additional UFH during PCI.
